artists.biography:
"The Anchoress is the Welsh multi-instrumentalist, songwriter and author Catherine Anne Davies (aka Catherine AD).
The Anchoress is the stage name of Welsh musician/songwriter Catherine Anne Davies, who also records under the nom de plume Catherine A.D. A self-taught multi-instrumentalist, chanteuse, and singer/songwriter specializing in a heady blend of gothic chamber pop and dark atmospheric art rock, Davies has drawn comparisons to PJ Harvey, Nick Cave, Anna Calvi, My Brightest Diamond, and Kate Bush. She issued a series of well-received independently released EPs before switching over to the Anchoress moniker in 2014 and issuing the single "One for Sorrow.. ~ James Christopher Monger
From March to Dec 2015, Davies performed in Simple Minds' live band, contributing additional guitar and keyboards. She met Jim Kerr through The Dark Flowers collective. She has also performed live with Ed Harcourt at Glastonbury Festival, as well as Martha Wainwright.
Davies has been described by NPR's Ann Powers as "Wales's (much more explicitly feminist) answer to Lana Del Rey."

perplexity.description:
The Art of Losing is the second studio album by Welsh multi-instrumentalist The Anchoress (Catherine Anne Davies), released on 12 March 2021 through Kscope. Musically, the album blends dark alt-pop with elements of indie rock and art-pop, characterized by moody pianos, cellos, synthesizers, and dynamic drum arrangements. The production is layered and atmospheric, supporting Davies’s emotionally charged songwriting. The album features guest appearances, most notably James Dean Bradfield of Manic Street Preachers, and draws inspiration from artists like Scott Walker, David Bowie, and the Manic Street Preachers.

As a follow-up to her acclaimed 2016 debut Confessions of a Romance Novelist, The Art of Losing marks The Anchoress’s first full-length solo release in five years. The album is a concept work centered on themes of grief, loss, fury, and personal trauma, with lyrics that reflect Davies’s own experiences. Upon its release, the album received widespread critical acclaim, appearing on several year-end lists from publications such as Prog, Classic Rock, and The Sunday Times, and earning recognition as HMV’s Welsh Album of the Year and a nominee for the Welsh Music Prize.
